content:
Facts: Four siblings contested their mother’s public will executed shortly before her death, alleging (i) natural incapacity of the testator, (ii) inducement to error by third parties in the formation of the testamentary will, and (iii) infringement of their legitimate shares. The will contained specific legacies of real estate to each child and a legacy of debt (acknowledgement of €100,000) in favour of one daughter for renovation works. The plaintiffs sought annulment/nullity of the will, alternatively reduction of the testamentary dispositions and reinstatement of their reserved shares. The defendants opposed, raised inadmissibility of the reduction action, and defended the validity and effectiveness of both the will and the debt legacy.

Legal framework
Articles 591, 624, 551, 552, 553–556, 537, 460 of the Italian Civil Code (capacity to make a will; inducement to error; legacies in lieu of or imputable to the legitimate portion; reduction; fictitious reunion; reserved shares); Articles 279(2)(5), 104(2), 183(6) of the Italian Code of Civil Procedure; principles on burden of proof in testamentary incapacity, interpretation of wills, admissibility of actions for reduction, and debt of value in reinstatement.

Issue
Whether the public will was invalid due to natural incapacity or inducement to error; whether the legacy of debt was valid and imputable as a debt of the estate; whether the action for reduction was admissible without prior renunciation of legacies; and whether, upon reconstruction of the estate, the testamentary dispositions infringed the legitimate shares of some heirs, requiring proportional reduction and monetary reinstatement.

Principle
Natural incapacity of the testator requires rigorous proof of a total inability to understand and will at the time of execution; serious illness or palliative treatment alone is insufficient absent clear evidence of complete cognitive impairment. Inducement to error under Article 624 c.c. requires proof of a causal misrepresentation affecting the testator’s will at the relevant time, which cannot be inferred solely from ex post discrepancies in asset valuation. In interpreting wills, the judge must ascertain the actual intent of the testator through an overall assessment, allowing attribution of non-literal meanings consistent with that intent. In the absence of an unequivocal intention to satisfy legitimate heirs exclusively through legacies, testamentary attributions are imputable to the legitimate portion (art. 552 c.c.), and the action for reduction is admissible without prior renunciation; in any event, such renunciation may validly be expressed through procedural acts. A legacy of debt acknowledging reimbursement for proven expenses constitutes a debt of the estate to be deducted in the fictitious reunion. Where reconstruction of the estate shows infringement of reserved shares, testamentary dispositions must be proportionally reduced, and reinstatement takes the form of a debt of value, subject to revaluation and statutory interest from the date of the claim. Cash devolved by law to the four heirs, consisting of:
€29,000.00 in credit securities at banca intesa, bormio branch;
€12,000.00 as the remaining balance in a current account at banca intesa, bormio branch;
Jewellery and precious items, valued at €5,467.00, deposited in a safety deposit box at the banca intesa branch in bormio;
Money amounting to €8,175.00 in cheques and cash, collected by the deceased as rent.
Donatum.
The court-appointed expert found no evidence of donations.
Aes alienum.
The court-appointed expert considered the bequest of €100,000.00 in favour of heir 3 (rectius, third party 2s.a.s.) To be an inheritance debt.
That being said, given that the relictum amounts to a total of €807,762.00, the donatum at 0 and the aes alienum at €100,000.00, the total value of the fictitiously reconstructed estate is €707,762.00 (p. 12 of the court-appointed expert's report).
In this regard, the defendants' objection that the debt legacy should be subtracted from the legitimate share rather than from the estate must be rejected, as it is a debt of the deceased and, therefore, of the entire estate, to be attributed to the latter pursuant to and for the purposes of article 553 of the italian civil code.
Ii) legitimate share, available share, shares for each legitimate heir.
Given that the legitimate heirs consist of four children of the deceased, pursuant to article 537, paragraph 2 of the italian civil code, they are entitled to two-thirds (2/3) of the estate, therefore 1/6 (=2/3:1/4) each.
It follows that:
Total value of the estate: €707,762.00. Available share: €235,920.00 (1/3).
Legitimate share: €471,841.00 (2/3).
Share reserved for each legitimate heir: €117,960.00 (1/6).
Iii) assessment of damage to legitimate shares.
In this regard, the testamentary provisions including the bequest of debt and the assets falling into succession by law assigned:
To the daughter heir 3:
The shop sheet .. Part. .. Sub 3 euros 506,000.00 1/4 of the cellar sheet .. Part. .. Sub 8 euros 1,400.00 1/4 of the cellar sheet .. Part. .. Sub 23 euros 1,750.00 1/12 of the pasture sheet .. Total value €428,640.50

Total value €166,640.50
To daughter heir 2:
Deposit in (omissis) sheet .. Part. .. €30,000.00 1/4 of the cellar sheet .. Part. .. Sub 8 €1,400.00 1/4 of the cellar sheet .. Part. .. Sub 23 €1,750.00 1/12 of the pasture sheet .. Part. .. €457.50 1/12 of the lawn sheet .. Part. .. €1,707.50 1/12 of the lawn sheet .. Total value €52,640.50
To daughter heir 1:

Part. .. Euro 457.50 1/12 of the meadow sheet .. Part. .. €1,707.50 1/12 of the meadow sheet .. Part. .. €3,665.00 1/4 credit securities at intesa bank 7,250.00 euros 1/4 remaining sum at intesa bank 3,000.00 euros 1/4 sum deposited in the safe deposit box €2,043.75 1/4 value of jewellery deposited in the safe deposit box €1,366.75
Total value €59,840.50
Based on the above assessments, considering that the share reserved for each legitimate heir amounts to €117,960.00, it is clear that the legitimate share has been infringed to the detriment of the plaintiffs heir 1 and heir 2. Specifically:
Heir 1 has suffered a total loss of (€117,960.00-59,840.50) €58,119.50
Heir 2 is owed a total of (€117,960.00-52,640.50) €65,319.50 (pp. 12-15 of the court-appointed expert's report).
Iv) reduction of testamentary dispositions and determination of reinstatements (pp. 16-18 of the court-appointed expert's report).
The appointed court-appointed expert correctly proceeded by assigning to the legitimate heirs heir 2 and heir 1 the entire shares of the assets falling into intestate succession, half to each, and completing the reinstatements by identifying cash adjustments, which the legatees heir 3 and heir 4 must pay in accordance with the proportional balance desired by the testator.
The inheritance devolved to the legatee heir 3, who received a bequest of €506,000.00, the recognition of a debt of €100,000.00 and a 1/4 share of the assets falling under intestate succession worth €22,640.50, for a total of €428,640.50, is reduced by the intestate entitlements.
The inheritance devolved to the legatee heir 4, who received a bequest worth €144,000.00 in addition to 1/4 of the assets falling under intestate succession worth €22,640.50, for a total of €166,640.50, is reduced by the intestate entitlements.
The inheritance devolved to the legatee heir 1, who received a bequest worth €37,200.00 and a share of 1/4 of the assets falling under intestate succession worth €22,640.50, for a total of €59,840.50, is supplemented with the 1/4 share of the intestate assets already assigned by law to her sister heir 3 (worth €22,640.50) and adjusted in cash by €35,479.00 until the full integration of the share reserved for her of €117,960.00.
The inheritance devolved to the legatee heir 2, who received a bequest worth €30,000.00 and 1/4 of the intestate assets worth €22,640.50 for a total of €52,640.50, is supplemented with 1/4 of the intestate assets already assigned by law to her brother heir 4 (worth €22,640.50) and adjusted in cash for €42,679.00 until the full integration of the share reserved for her of €117,960.00.
The cash supplements previously identified, totalling €78,158.00 (=€35,479.00 + €42,679.00), will be paid by the legatees heir 3 and heir 4 in proportion to the donations made by the deceased: therefore, considering thatheir 3 inherited a value of €406,000.00, consisting of the legitimate share of €117,960.00 and part of the available share of €288,040.00, and heir 4 inherited a value of €144,000.00 - consisting of the legitimate share of €117,960.00 and part of the available share of €26,040.00 - it follows that the reinstatement must be paid by the legatees heir 3 and heir 4 in proportion to the available inheritance, i.e. Heir 3 must pay €71,102.00 and heir 4 €7,056.00.
Further considerations on the failure to include two cellars in the building in (omissis) in the legacies, included by the court-appointed expert in the intestate succession (see point i), and on the net annual return on the properties subject to reinstatement, are ancillary issues relevant to the further request for division, which are not the subject of this judgment.
In view of the above, the following is ordered:
Heir 3 to reinstate the plaintiffs' legitimate shares, for a total amount of €71,102.00;
Heir 4 to reinstate the plaintiffs' legitimate shares, for a total amount of €7,056.00.
With regard to interest, reference is made to established case law according to which reinstatement represents a debt of value and therefore 'must be adjusted to the changed value - to the
At the time of the judicial decision, the asset to which the legitimate heir would be entitled, so that it constitutes the exact equivalent, must therefore be revalued on the basis of the variation in the istat indices on the cost of living and, in the case of interest-bearing assets, the payment of the 'fruits' not received by the legitimate heir (in this case, compensatory interest on the revalued sum) to be arranged from the date of the application" (ex multis, cass. 19.5.2005 no. 10564), in the present case, the sums subject to reinstatement must be devalued at the date of the opening of the succession (26.3.2015), when the injury occurred, and gradually revalued until the publication of this judgment. The sums gradually revalued are subject to statutory interest from the dates of notification of the claims for reduction/reinstatement of each aggrieved legitimate heir until the actual balance is paid: in particular, for heir 3 from 27.7.2017 and for heir 4 from 21.8.2017 (see notifications of the writ of summons).
legal costs
Considering the nature and particular sensitivity of the subject matter of the dispute, as well as the mutual defeat of the parties (for the plaintiffs: rejection of the claims pursuant to article 591 of the italian civil code, pursuant to article 624 of the italian civil code and ascertainment of the existence of the debt legacy; for the defendants: rejection of the objection of inadmissibility of the action for reduction, rejection of the objections regarding donations and removal of assets; ascertainment of a not insignificant infringement of the plaintiffs' legitimate shares), there are justified grounds for ordering the full compensation of the costs of the proceedings.
Similarly, the costs of the court-appointed expert, settled by separate decree dated 29 march 2019, are definitively borne jointly by the parties.
P.q.m.
The court, sitting as a panel, having rejected or absorbed all other claims and objections, in relation to the estate of the deceased, who died with a will in bormio on ..., in granting the request for reduction, having ascertained the value of the fictitiously reunited estate,
Finds that the legitimate heirs heir 1 and heir 2 have suffered a loss of their respective reserved shares as specified in the grounds in paragraph c iii) and, having applied the reduction of the prejudicial testamentary provisions specified in the grounds in paragraph c iv), as a result,
Orders heir 3 to reinstate the plaintiffs' legitimate shares by paying them the total sum of €71,102.00; on the aforementioned sum, devalued to 26 march 2015 and revalued until the publication of this judgment, is subject to statutory interest from 27 july 2017 until the actual balance is paid;
Orders heir 4 to reinstate the plaintiffs' legitimate shares by paying them the total sum of €7,056.00; on the aforementioned sum, devalued as at 26 march 2015 and revalued until the publication of this judgment, statutory interest is due from 21 august 2017 until the actual balance is paid;
Rejects all other claims and objections, except for the claim for division and related ancillary claims, for which provision is made in point 5;
Compensates the parties in full for the costs of the proceedings;
Definitively orders the parties to bear jointly and severally the costs of the court-appointed expert, settled by separate decree dated 29 march 2019;
Having regard to articles 279(2)(5) and 104(2) of the italian code of civil procedure, orders the separation of the proceedings limited to the request for division and related ancillary claims and remands the case for preliminary investigation, as per separate order.
Sondrio, chambers of 19 july 2021.
